title: Who Really Got Paid for $6 Eggs?
summary: In March 2025, a dozen eggs in America cost a record $6.23. By October 2026, it was $2.32. Bird flu was the official explanation, and it was real. But in June 2026, the Justice Department and 17 states accused three of the biggest egg producers of pushing up a price most Americans have never heard of: the Urner Barry benchmark. We follow one dozen eggs from the hen to the shelf, through the virus, the benchmark, the alleged bids, the record profits, the crash to 22 cents wholesale, and the supermarket price that fell much more slowly. The companies denied wrongdoing and settled without admitting any. Main sources below.
